execution_evidence.reason: Allocation code, integration tests, and benchmark runner are defined and committed but have not been compiled/executed here. Exact-head Rust/TLA+ receipts and multi-agent qualification remain outstanding.

claim_ceiling: Reference-model conformance only when executed against a named source revision.
Does not prove Holochain DHT integrity, key custody, real-world service delivery, legal tender status, reserve adequacy, FX parity, or external settlement finality.
Does not prove that production zomes enforce the same properties until separately qualified against exact source and multi-agent runtime evidence.

invariants.name: Instrument identity is not ticker identity
invariants.statement: Distinct canonical instrument IDs remain distinct even when symbol, display name, or numeric amount is identical.

invariants.name: Canonical profile binding
invariants.statement: Authorization and value mutations resolve instrument properties from a canonical registry; a caller cannot supply an alternate profile at the operation boundary.

invariants.name: Action-scoped authority
invariants.statement: A capability is valid only for its exact issuer, delegate, instrument, action, current revision, expiry, and declared amount ceiling.

invariants.name: Mutual-credit conservation
invariants.statement: Each accepted mutual-credit event changes provider and receiver positions by equal and opposite amounts within that instrument.

invariants.name: Atomic rejection
invariants.statement: A rejected event changes neither balances, outstanding obligations, nor consumed event IDs.

invariants.name: Idempotent replay
invariants.statement: An exact retry has one effect; reusing an event ID with a different payload is rejected.

invariants.name: Bounded federation exposure
invariants.statement: Outstanding obligations remain within each peering-edge cap and any configured aggregate gross-exposure cap scoped to that exact instrument; raw amounts from unlike instruments are never summed.

invariants.name: Risk stop with safe unwind
invariants.statement: Pausing new obligations blocks new exposure while allowing separately authorized settlement of already-incurred obligations.

invariants.name: Denomination stability
invariants.statement: An instrument ID cannot silently change its denomination identity or scale; migration requires a new instrument identity or an explicit qualified migration.

invariants.name: Same-revision profile consistency
invariants.statement: A profile's policy fields cannot change without a revision change; revisioned updates must preserve immutable issuer, family, and denomination semantics.

invariants.name: Aggregate exposure is instrument-scoped
invariants.statement: Aggregate gross exposure compares amounts only within the same canonical instrument/unit domain; unlike currencies require a separately qualified conversion/risk model before risk-value aggregation.

invariants.name: Gross obligations do not implicitly net
invariants.statement: Opposing directional obligations remain separately outstanding by default. Signed net position is diagnostic only and may not substitute for gross exposure limits; settlement must identify the direction being reduced. Netting requires a separately qualified agreement and enforcement path.

invariants.name: Clearing agreements bind a canonical instrument profile
invariants.statement: A clearing agreement can be created only for a registered instrument and pins the exact profile revision. Unknown IDs and stale profile revisions fail closed; non-transferable reputation-family instruments cannot be used as spendable clearing instruments.

invariants.name: Partitioned exposure rights are preallocated and non-overlapping
invariants.statement: During disconnected operation, each shard may consume only its previously allocated reservation. Reservation slices across shards, agreements and epochs are counted against the exact community/instrument cap; prior-epoch slices are not reclaimed without coordinated fencing/reconciliation.

invariants.name: Reservation agreement identity binds counterparties
invariants.statement: A reservation agreement ID identifies one immutable community pair across instruments, shards, and epochs. Budget slices cannot be reassigned to a different counterparty pair by reusing the agreement identifier.

invariants.name: Fence precedes transfer
invariants.statement: A successor allocation cannot become spendable until the prior epoch has a verifiable fencing decision in the authoritative control chain.

invariants.name: One active owner per allocation epoch
invariants.statement: Every spendable allocation has exactly one owner under the verified control chain; old and successor epochs cannot both create accepted exposure against the same rights.

invariants.name: No timeout-only reallocation
invariants.statement: A timeout, missed heartbeat or local clock comparison alone cannot reclaim risk rights from a potentially live owner.

invariants.name: Complete reconciliation before transfer
invariants.statement: If the accepted operation set through the terminal cut or pending exposure is unresolved, transferable capacity is unknown and no transfer may succeed.

invariants.name: Risk-right transfer is conserved
invariants.statement: A transferred unit is debited from the old allocation and credited to at most one successor allocation in a recoverable control-plane transition.

invariants.name: Receipts are canonical and payload-bound
invariants.statement: Receipts bind scope, instrument/profile, caps/policy revisions, owner, epoch, predecessor and payload digest; exact retries are idempotent and conflicting reuse fails closed.

invariants.name: Stale policy revisions cannot transfer rights
invariants.statement: Instrument, community-cap or agreement-cap revision mismatch blocks transfer unless an explicit authorized migration is qualified.

invariants.name: Crash recovery preserves last verified state
invariants.statement: Recovery after any failed transition does not create duplicated spendable capacity or advance beyond the last verified committed control receipt.

invariants.name: Ledger and control operations share one idempotency namespace
invariants.statement: A monetary event ID cannot alias a drain, fencing, or transfer receipt ID; every transition ID is globally unique within the allocation reference model and payload-bound.

invariants.name: Aggregate reservation rights are non-overlapping across shards
invariants.statement: For each exact capacity/instrument domain, the sum of shard reservations never exceeds the configured aggregate budget; every shard's outstanding exposure remains within its own allocated slice, including during partitioned operation.

invariants.name: Shard allocation rights are frozen during a partition
invariants.statement: After a partition begins, the reserved-capacity vector for the affected budget domain remains unchanged until the partition heals or an explicitly coordinated fencing/reconciliation protocol authorizes reallocation.

invariants.name: Lost-response retry preserves the original economic effect
invariants.statement: After a transfer is durably committed but its response is lost, retrying the same canonical transfer ID and payload returns the original receipt and creates no additional capacity or commit.

invariants.name: Conflicting idempotency payloads are rejected
invariants.statement: Reusing a committed transfer ID with any changed canonical payload is rejected, returns no success receipt, and produces no economic mutation.

invariants.name: Replay protection outlives the declared offline horizon
invariants.statement: A committed operation ID or replay-prevention tombstone is retained until every protocol-defined stale-owner and offline-replay condition has been closed. If the safe replay horizon is unknown, the ID is not recycled.

invariants.name: Static allocation conserves the risk budget
invariants.statement: Contingency reserve plus the sum of all static shard rights equals the total configured capacity, with no overflow or overspend.

invariants.name: Static allocation is canonical and deterministic
invariants.statement: The same canonical shard demands, minima, policy parameters, capacity and seed-independent input produce identical per-shard rights regardless of input order; deterministic tie breaks use stable shard IDs.

invariants.name: Forecast signals never authorize partition-time reallocation
invariants.statement: Historical demand samples affect only the pre-partition allocation plan. The allocator cannot mutate active rights or reclaim an unreachable owner's reservation.

conformance_cases.title: Bounded capability accepts an in-limit action
Capability cannot be used by a different actor or for an ungranted action
conformance_cases.attack: Impersonate the named delegate or reuse a capability for another action.

conformance_cases.title: Amount ceiling fails closed when amount is missing
conformance_cases.attack: Call a mutation with a bounded capability but omit the amount.

conformance_cases.title: Negative amount cannot bypass a ceiling
conformance_cases.attack: Submit a negative amount where a bounded operation is expected.

conformance_cases.title: Unbounded issuance capability is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt issuance without a declared maximum amount.

conformance_cases.title: Inactive instrument rejects new issuance
conformance_cases.attack: Issue while instrument is inactive, using a capability matching the registered issuer and revision.

conformance_cases.title: Paused or inactive instrument can permit separately authorized settlement
Duplicate ticker does not alias distinct instruments
conformance_cases.attack: Register two distinct instrument IDs with the same display symbol.

conformance_cases.title: Reusing an instrument ID with another issuer is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Register an existing canonical instrument ID under an attacker-controlled issuer.

conformance_cases.title: Mutual-credit event conserves net position
Stale profile revision cannot authorize a new mutation
conformance_cases.attack: Submit an event created for revision N to a registry that contains revision N+1.

conformance_cases.title: Wrong instrument family cannot use mutual-credit operations
conformance_cases.attack: Use a resource-credit profile in the mutual-credit exchange API.

conformance_cases.title: Balance limit rejection is atomic
conformance_cases.attack: Submit an exchange that would exceed a participant balance limit.

conformance_cases.title: Same event ID and same payload is idempotent
conformance_cases.attack: Retry an already accepted event without changing its payload.

conformance_cases.title: Same event ID with changed payload is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse an accepted exchange ID with a changed amount.

conformance_cases.title: Per-edge exposure limit is enforced
conformance_cases.attack: Increase one peering obligation beyond its bilateral cap.

conformance_cases.title: Aggregate gross exposure across edges is enforced
conformance_cases.attack: Commit exposure on one federation edge, then overcommit aggregate capacity through another edge.

conformance_cases.title: Rejected over-cap event ID is not consumed
conformance_cases.attack: Retry the same event ID with a valid in-cap amount after an over-cap attempt is rejected.

conformance_cases.title: Stale agreement revision is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Post an obligation using a revision other than the registered agreement revision.

conformance_cases.title: Pause blocks new obligations but permits existing settlement
Settlement cannot exceed outstanding obligation
conformance_cases.attack: Settle a value greater than the remaining signed obligation.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement retry is idempotent and payload-bound
conformance_cases.attack: Retry a settlement ID once with the same payload and once with a changed amount.

conformance_cases.title: Same instrument ID cannot silently change unit or scale
conformance_cases.attack: Present a same-ID, same-revision profile with changed denomination semantics after balances exist.

conformance_cases.title: Same-revision credit-limit widening is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Present a registry profile with the same instrument ID and revision but a more permissive balance limit after a previous operation.

conformance_cases.title: Revisioned policy update preserves instrument identity and denomination
Aggregate exposure does not sum raw amounts across unlike instruments
conformance_cases.attack: Open an obligation in another instrument while a same-instrument peer-edge cap is nearly or fully used.

conformance_cases.title: New obligations require explicit aggregate caps for both communities
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt a new obligation when either involved community has not configured an aggregate cap for the exact instrument.

conformance_cases.title: A zero aggregate cap explicitly blocks new exposure
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt a new obligation when one community has explicitly set the exact instrument's aggregate cap to zero.

conformance_cases.title: Rejected missing-cap and zero-cap attempts do not consume event identity
conformance_cases.attack: Retry the identical event ID after both communities install a positive, adequate cap; it must apply once, not be stuck as a phantom prior event.

conformance_cases.title: Opposing obligations do not silently net against gross-exposure caps
conformance_cases.attack: Record an obligation from A to B followed by a reverse obligation from B to A; risk checks must use the sum of both unsettled directions, not the signed net.

conformance_cases.title: Clearing agreement cannot reference an unregistered instrument
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to create a peer clearing agreement for an instrument ID absent from the canonical registry.

conformance_cases.title: Clearing agreement must pin the current instrument profile revision
conformance_cases.attack: Create an agreement whose instrument_revision differs from the canonical registry's profile revision.

conformance_cases.title: Non-transferable reputation cannot be used as a spendable clearing instrument
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to bind a reputation-family instrument such as MYCEL to a clearing agreement.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement reduces only the explicitly selected obligation direction
conformance_cases.attack: Create outstanding obligations in both directions and submit a settlement for only one direction; verify the opposite direction remains outstanding.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement event identity is bound to direction
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse a settlement ID with the same amount and agreement but the opposite direction; the retry must reject instead of settling a different obligation leg.

conformance_cases.title: Partitioned shards cannot exceed their pre-allocated gross-risk slices
conformance_cases.attack: Two disconnected writers attempt to consume more than their disjoint reservations collectively permit.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation allocation requires explicit community and agreement caps
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to reserve capacity before either involved community or the agreement has a configured cap.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement restores reusable capacity only within its own reservation
conformance_cases.attack: Settle 40 units on shard A, then attempt to use 61 units on shard B whose reservation is 60; only A's own reservation may reuse the released 40.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation caps are not summed across unlike instrument units
conformance_cases.attack: Allocate separate hour and water units for the same communities and verify that each exact instrument has its own cap.

conformance_cases.title: Old-epoch reservation remains charged until explicit coordinated rebalancing
conformance_cases.attack: Try to allocate the same capacity to a new epoch while the old reservation has not been retired/fenced.

conformance_cases.title: Explicit zero community or agreement cap prevents reservations
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to allocate a positive shard reservation when either community cap or the agreement cap is zero.

conformance_cases.title: Event ID cannot be replayed against another shard reservation
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse an accepted event ID with a different reservation key/shard; the conflicting replay must reject with no second obligation.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation slices preserve one immutable counterparty pair per agreement ID
conformance_cases.attack: Try to reserve another shard or instrument under an existing agreement ID but substitute one community; the shared identifier must not silently represent a different bilateral agreement.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Mutual-credit conservation, throughput, and idempotency stress
benchmark_campaigns.target: 0 net-position drift and exactly one state effect per unique event
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the exact-head wrapper on a clean checkout. Keep the JSON output and receipt SHA-256. Repeat with multiple recorded seeds and matched hardware/toolchains before comparative claims.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Federation scale and partition behavior
benchmark_campaigns.reservation_reference_harness_claim_ceil: Single-process deterministic reservation-model benchmark only; does not measure network partitions, true concurrent writers, Holochain/DHT, external settlement or distributed fencing.
benchmark_campaigns.reservation_reference_harness_methodolog: Run the clean-checkout wrapper at the exact committed revision with 2+ shards, several fixed seeds, matched toolchain/hardware, and retain the JSON plus binary/output receipt digests. Compare utilization and latency alongside cap-rejection correctness; do not treat unused reserved capacity as free capacity.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Comparative institutional welfare and risk vector
benchmark_campaigns.method: Matched workload and shock traces, fixed and held-out shocks, multiple recorded seeds, ablations, and independent recomputation. Do not collapse metrics into one score.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Partitioned-risk fencing state-machine model checking
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: A deterministic state-machine/model-checker result only for the declared authority and fault model. It does not prove production Holochain behavior, legal settlement, cryptographic key security or safety outside the explored model.
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the bounded NCF-FEN safe lifecycle model and the NCF-ESCROW two-shard safe model at Capacity=2 and four operation steps; require both to complete without invariant violations. The escrow model freezes its reservation vector during a partition. Then require four unsafe mutants to be detected specifically: timeout-only reallocation -> NoTransferWithoutFence; stale-owner write after transfer -> NoOldWriteOutsideActive; duplicate full-budget allocation across shards -> ReservedCapacityBound; resizing a shard's reservation during a partition -> PartitionedReservationsStayFixed. Parser/tool failures do not count as detection. These results are not yet confirmed. Then qualify the independent transition oracle and exhaust small interleavings. Extend with at least 10,000 reproducible schedules for retries, duplicate/reordered/dropped receipts, stale-owner writes, crashes and partition/heal traces. Keep honest-crash and adversarial-owner campaigns separate. Compare static-quota, acknowledged-drain and any linearizable/quorum mode under identical traces. Any safety violation fails the campaign; utilization and latency are reported only alongside correctness results. The fail-closed runner requires a clean checkout and caller-supplied TLA2TOOLS_JAR; it records source/model/config/JAR hashes and raw logs outside the repository.
benchmark_campaigns.workflow_claim_ceiling: The dedicated draft-PR workflow checks two finite TLA+ models and sensitivity to four deliberately unsafe mutants only; it does not qualify the Rust implementation, distributed concurrency, Holochain validators, or 10,000-schedule model checking.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Safety-qualified liquidity and capacity-utilization frontier
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the exact same deterministic demand/fault traces against each implemented policy and matched hardware/toolchains. Report results only after hard safety gates pass. Plot a Pareto frontier across economic demand served, safely reclaimable versus stranded capacity, tail latency, and compute cost; do not collapse outcomes into a single weighted score. Separate unreachable-owner partitions from honest crash/restart and byzantine-owner campaigns. Include ablations for priority classes and rebalancing policy. Add a low-risk paradigm-shift baseline: optimize the placement of already-authorized, non-overlapping slices before the partition, using training demand traces and robust quantiles. Evaluate on held-out and shifted workloads, and never allow the forecast to enlarge/reassign rights during the partition. This isolates safe capacity-placement improvements from risky online reclamation. An executable dependency-free Rust allocator and benchmark were added. It uses checked integer arithmetic, stable shard-ID tie-breaking, and largest-remainder apportionment; the benchmark compares three policies on the same generated stationary and shifted trace sets. Its current generator is synthetic and single-process. Run the exact-head wrapper, then replace/augment synthetic traces with independently sourced demand profiles before making real-world claims.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: A future passing Rust reference model + synthetic matched-trace simulation only. It does not qualify distributed races, partition-time reallocation, Holochain, demand forecasts from real populations, solvency, or production economic welfare.

reservation_policy_experiment.hypothesis: Demand-aware allocation of non-overlapping rights before a partition can improve economic demand served without relaxing partition safety or requiring any partition-time reallocation.
reservation_policy_experiment.evaluation: Train allocation weights only on recorded training traces; evaluate on held-out and distribution-shift traces. Report per-shard unserved demand, safe capacity usage, fragmented/unused quota, forecast error, and essential-service demand served. Any safety violation disqualifies the policy regardless of utilization.
reservation_policy_experiment.claim_boundary: An optimization of pre-authorized quota placement, not a method for safely reclaiming an unreachable owner's active rights.

policies.description: Equal integer weights after explicit minimums
Ceiling mean of historical integer demand samples
Nearest-rank 95th percentile plus a 25% proportional margin

evaluation_modes.description: Held-out samples from the historical shard demand shape with bounded jitter and bursts
Held-out samples after rotating the demand propensity across shards, to expose stale-history fragility

planned_conformance_cases.title: Timeout alone does not reclaim capacity
planned_conformance_cases.attack: A shard misses its heartbeat but is still potentially live; a different owner requests its slice.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Stale owner write after a verified fence rejects
planned_conformance_cases.attack: An owner submits a new obligation referencing an epoch closed by a valid fencing receipt.

planned_conformance_cases.title: New owner cannot spend before transfer commit
planned_conformance_cases.attack: The successor presents an allocation proposal but no verifiable committed transfer receipt.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Unresolved terminal operation set prevents transfer
planned_conformance_cases.attack: One dependency or operation through the proposed terminal watermark is unavailable.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Conflicting receipt replay rejects
planned_conformance_cases.attack: A receipt ID is reused with a changed owner, amount, epoch, predecessor or policy digest.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Crash at every transition cannot double-allocate
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Inject a crash after each durable step of drain, reconcile, fence, prepare, debit, credit and commit.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Cap or instrument revision change blocks stale transfer
planned_conformance_cases.attack: A relevant cap or profile revision changes after the allocation snapshot was read.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Last-unit race accepts at most one claimant
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Race 100 attempts against one remaining unit using the selected control authority.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Unreachable owner retains charged capacity without an authoritative fence
planned_conformance_cases.attack: The old owner is partitioned and cannot provide a drain acknowledgement; no qualified linearizable/quorum fence is available.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Receipt reordering converges deterministically
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Deliver valid receipt dependencies out of order and then make all required dependencies available.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Unknown pending exposure makes transferable amount unknown
planned_conformance_cases.attack: The terminal outstanding amount is known but one possible in-flight operation cannot be reconciled.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Prepare/commit recovery never frees capacity between owners
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Interrupt transfer between old-allocation debit and new-allocation credit, then run deterministic recovery.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Ledger events cannot alias lifecycle receipt IDs
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Reuse the same identifier across a ledger obligation or settlement and a drain, fence, or transfer control operation.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Independent formal checker detects timeout-only reallocation
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Use the deliberately unsafe timeout mutant to transfer risk capacity while the prior owner is merely draining and before reconciliation or fencing.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Independent formal checker detects stale-owner writes after transfer
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Run a deliberately unsafe mutant that lets the previous owner create a new obligation after a successor allocation has become active.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Independent formal checker detects duplicate full-budget allocation across shards
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Use a deliberately unsafe allocation action that gives a second shard the entire aggregate capacity while a first shard already owns a non-zero slice.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Ten thousand deterministic lifecycle variants preserve the aggregate exposure bound
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Generate 10,000 reproducible combinations of capacity, old exposure, settlements, pending exposure, reconciliation failures, transfer attempts, and successor spends. Every accepted state must preserve the exact aggregate capacity bound.
planned_conformance_cases.claim_ceiling: Deterministic generated sequential Rust reference-model regression only; not concurrent interleavings, exhaustive formal proof, or Holochain multi-agent evidence.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Independent formal checker detects reservation resizing during a partition
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Mutate a shard's allocated slice while the model is partitioned, despite the protocol requiring reservation rights to remain frozen.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Lost transfer response retry returns the original committed receipt
planned_conformance_cases.attack: The transfer commit is durable, the acknowledgement is lost, and the caller retries with the same transfer ID and canonical amount payload, including after a crash/restart.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Same transfer ID with a different amount payload is rejected
planned_conformance_cases.attack: After the original commit response is lost, an adversary or buggy client reuses the transfer ID with a changed amount payload.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Lost commit acknowledgement across restart cannot duplicate a transfer
planned_conformance_cases.attack: A transfer commits durably, the process crashes before the caller observes success, then the process restarts and the same transfer is retried.

planned_conformance_cases.title: A long-offline member cannot replay a transfer after short-lived idempotency cache expiry
planned_conformance_cases.attack: A community remains partitioned beyond the normal online retry window, reconnects later, and resubmits a previously committed transfer using its old operation ID.
planned_conformance_cases.rationale: This requires a persistence/replay-horizon model; a bounded lifecycle model with no time or tombstone-retention state does not qualify it.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Equal split conserves awkward integer capacity with stable tie breaks
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Allocate an odd capacity across an uneven shard count; permute the input list and compare per-shard results.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Demand-weighted allocation follows canonical integer weights
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Provide demand means in a known ratio and verify integer allocation and exact total capacity.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Robust quantile allocation applies explicit quantile and margin
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Provide outlier-bearing samples and a known percentile/margin; verify weight values and resulting slices.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Contingency reserve remains unallocated
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Request a nonzero reserve and verify no shard receives the reserved capacity.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Static allocation plan is invariant to input order
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Permute the same canonical demand samples and shard IDs across every policy.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Insufficient minimum slices fail closed
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Set per-shard minimums above the spendable budget after contingency reserve.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Malformed demand history cannot overflow the allocator
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Provide integer samples whose accumulation overflows the chosen representation.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Demand policy frontier is measured under stationary and shifted traces
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Fit slice weights to a stationary training profile then evaluate all policies on matched stationary and rotated-profile traces.

planned_conformance_cases.title: Planned static allocation slices are accepted by the reservation reference without crossing caps
planned_conformance_cases.attack: Allocate a budget with a contingency reserve, then reserve every returned slice against both community caps and the agreement cap.

qualification_campaigns.name: Exact-head Rust reference-model qualification
qualification_campaigns.method: Run format, tests, and clippy independently; continue after a failed check so the receipt captures all three outcomes. Require the overall result to pass only when all checks pass. Checkout is exact-head, the worktree must be clean, CARGO_TARGET_DIR and logs live outside the checkout, and the receipt binds the source commit/tree, manifest/lock/source digests, compiler identity and per-check log digests.
qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Formatting, tests and clippy for the exact standalone Rust reference crate only. Does not establish distributed/Holochain safety, cryptographic fencing, external settlement finality or production ledger correctness.

qualification_campaigns.name: Deterministic generated fencing lifecycle sweep
invariants_checked: new exposure is rejected after drain/fence
failed transfer and spend attempts do not consume idempotency identity
transferred slice does not exceed verified free capacity
old outstanding + unresolved pending + successor outstanding never exceeds aggregate capacity
successor outstanding never exceeds successor reservation
qualification_campaigns.method: A dependency-free deterministic LCG selects small capacities, initial gross exposure, settlements before/during drain, exposure extensions, pending exposure, and successor spend amounts. All 10,000 generated scenarios execute through FenceBook and assert the aggregate capacity relation. The fixed seed is stored in source. This is sequential generated testing, not a concurrent schedule explorer; it must be complemented by TLC and multi-agent fault tests.
qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Generated sequential Rust reference-model stress only; not distributed/Holochain concurrency safety or production settlement proof.
qualification_campaigns.note: The Rust qualification runner now records the fixed seed and 10,000 scenario target in its receipt. This is declared campaign metadata; only the test log and exit status from an actual exact-head run can establish whether it executed and passed.

qualification_campaigns.name: Exact-head crash/recovery and payload-bound transfer retry qualification
required_outcomes: safe model passes all configured invariants
qualification_campaigns.methodology: Run the safe finite recovery model and each negative control independently using the pinned TLA+ tools build. Require the named invariant violation for each mutant; parser, module-resolution and generic tool failures do not count. Preserve raw traces and bind the receipts to exact source/model/config/tool hashes.
qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Bounded TLA+ result only for declared atomic-durable transition semantics and finite bounds. It does not prove backend durability, production Holochain behavior, cryptographic authorization, or unbounded distributed safety.
qualification_campaigns.receipt_sha256_method: Compute SHA-256 over the closed receipt file and record it in runner stdout / workflow summary or artifact metadata; do not put a self-hash inside the receipt body.

qualification_campaigns.name: Exact-head static allocation unit tests and matched-trace frontier
qualification_campaigns.safety_gate: Every allocation plan validates and every policy/mode report must have zero accounting violations; any overflow, malformed input, or unaccounted capacity fails the campaign.
qualification_campaigns.receipt_sha256_method: SHA-256 of the closed receipt file, reported externally by runner stdout/workflow metadata; do not put self-hash inside the receipt.
qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Unit tests plus synthetic single-process matched-trace evaluation only; real-demand validity and distributed/Holochain safety remain separate.
